task: Stop the LiteLLM proxy path from attributing personal-budget-fallback spend to the named X-CodeMie-Project, so each request lands in exactly one ledger budget, with member and non-member regression tests.

key_reasoning.reason: Acceptance criteria are concrete, but the ticket contradicts the documented EPMCDME-15204 decision in the ledger's personal predicate (double count accepted as intended). The non-member premise only holds for admin/maintainer non-members and for members without a category allocation, and three scope questions are open: whether the own-credentials bypass path is in scope, header-level vs predicate-level fix, and whether stored historical rows stay as they are.

The closest pattern is the platform path (llm_factory _record_direct_budget_attribution plus _project_in_context), which already suppresses the project on fallback, so the proxy fix in _proxy_project_in_context is copy-and-adapt. The risk is billing and ledger correctness: dropping codemie_project changes attr_form/attr_project for fallback rows, and every attr_project consumer (ProjectHolder, member/group holders, access narrowing, hourly rollup) reads those columns. No auth or security surface changes. Existing proxy-router and spend-metadata transport test templates cover the member/non-member assertions, so no defensive-test bump applies.

One component: the enterprise LiteLLM proxy router's spend-logs metadata helper, plus its tests. A predicate-level change in spend_logs_repository is possible but is flagged as the riskier alternative, not the expected path.

Expected changes: proxy_router.py, test_proxy_router.py, test_spend_logs_metadata_transport.py, and possibly a docstring update in spend_logs_repository.py. That is 3-4 modified files and 0-1 new. Calibration matches the bundled S example epmcdme-10102 (3 files, total 11) and falls short of the M example epmcdme-10203 (6 files, three layers).
